All the rest can wait!!
Dec 2014 • Friends
The food in this restaurant is excellent. I can't honestly say it's the best in HCMC as many do, because I haven't eaten in every restaurant in HCMC. However, if you want fresh, tasty, clean, delicious food, served by an outstanding staff, then you need to come and enjoy. It's right on the edge of the canal, at the end of Truong Dinh St. On the night four of us came to eat, the owner was out and about, making sure that everything was just right, and I got the sense that he really wanted everyone to thoroughly enjoy themselves. Very accommodating, great service, excellent prices, and what more could you ask for? As a famous Governor once said, "I'll be back."

Very Good Vietnamese Food
Sep 2014 • Couples
If you want very good Vietnamese food in Ho Chi Minh City and don't want to spend an arm and a leg for the meal, this is the place to go. The restaurant on the left is better than their pub on the right (as you face the place) although they supposedly feed from the same kitchen. The Pub is much noisier, perhaps catering to a younger more boisterous crowd.
Fish stuffed with egg is a great dish, as is their fried calamari rings. It is good to come there early when the chef can devote more time to the food, because once the three floors of the restaurant, the outdoor seating, and the pub all fill up, the kitchen exhibits slight signs of stress. If you save room, the ice cream is superb, and if you don't save room, order it anyway. Just a taste is worth the whole price. This is a restaurant that is off the track beaten by tourists, but on one of the busiest corners in the city. We had to cross the street and needed an escort by the manager to make it, altho my wife is Vietnamese and I am a six year veteran of crossing Saigon Streets. We watched an ambulance stuck in the traffic and remarked that the person inside would probably die. Nobody here yields to ambulances. Sad.

Clean Local Food Restaurant with Reasonable Prices. Highly Recommanded!
Sep 2014 • Friends
As an expatriate in HCM city, I have to take my home-country colleagues who frequently come to Vietnam to lunch and dinner. It's always been a big headache to find different clean and cheap restaurants serving local foods every time. Then my local colleagues recommend Quan Dat, a restaurant barely mentioned in guide books and websites. And we all love it! It's a clean restaurants a bit far from downtown. You cannot miss Banh Canh, which everyone would have in the restaurant. Its Banh Xeo is also highly recommended; it's smaller than other restaurants in HCM city (according to my local colleague it's Nha Trang Style). What we loved most is octopus deep fried with fish sauce (actually I cannot recall it's octopus or squid in the menu). Sometimes we need to wait a while for the dish; the fish sauce brought a unique sweet tastes to the octopus and it's worth the time. Chicken wings with fish sauce is good too, even though it's bonier and thus less tasty than Quan 46A at Dinh Cong Trang (which is famous for Banh Xeo and chicken wings with fish sauce). My local colleagues recommends the fish noodles, but we think it's bland comparing to the above mentioned dishes.
 Waiters cannot speak English; the menu has English on it and it's not problem for foreigners. Waiters are very amiable and they will try every body language to make sure you have the food in correct ways (such as dipping correct sauces or wrapping Banh Canh/Banh Xeo with vegetables). When waiters cannot answer our questions, sometime they will find the owner who is the same amiable but can speak English.
 By the way, the address shall be 106 Troung Dinh in Q3.
